Simon: Heads-up — after the recent kernel-selection tweak I’m seeing a 15-25% tail-latency regression on the dedicated KV path. Need an nsys capture that shows kernel timelines + thread scheduling (OSRT) so we can correlate evictions with stalls. Anyone able to run a focused trace?

Maria: I can run one. Do you want full-run or bracketed capture? file sizes blow up if we record everything. :eyes:

Simon: Bracketed. The noisy window is around request burst + subsequent KV cleanup ~20–40s into a 60s test. NVTX ranges around infer:batch_start/batch_end are already annotated. Use NVTX to limit capture.

Jake: Quick recommended command I use for those cases (keeps file size reasonable and includes scheduling):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start="infer:batch_start" --capture-range-end="infer:batch_end" \
  --sample=cpu --sample-frequency=1000 --duration=60 -o kv-stall-$(date +%s)
```
Notes: --sample=cpu gives OS thread stacks, osrt capture shows runtime spin/wakeup events, and NVTX brackets avoid whole-run capture.

Anya: Also add `--cpuctx` or equivalent so we can see user-space stacks for the thread that does KV eviction — helped us find a spin-loop before. If file still big, drop `--sample-frequency` to 200 or capture just the problematic PID with `--target-pid`.

Maria: Running now (will push to s3 when done). Running with slight variant: `--sample-frequency=500` and `--capture-range-start`/end slightly expanded (+200ms) to catch pre/post behaviour.

Simon: If you spot kernel hop patterns (small kernels executing very frequently) we should grep for many tiny cuLaunchKernel calls and compare which kernel variant was chosen. That helped last time when QuantizedMatMul_4bit was chosen over fused GEMM and caused extra memcpy overhead.

Jake: FYI, when I tried short ~5s samples earlier they missed the eviction spike — sampling window too short. Aim for 30–90s depending on variability. For our bursts 60s is sweet spot.

perf-bot: Capture uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/kvcache/kv-stall-1938765432.nsight (70MB). Link: https://s3.redwood/kvcache/kv-stall-1938765432.nsight

Anya: I pulled it and opened the timeline. Quick tips for triage: 1) Filter timeline by `osrt` lanes to see thread wakeups; 2) Look at NVTX stack under the long idle on the worker thread — there’s an eviction path that runs on the main loop; 3) Use the API trace to see which model invocation triggered the eviction.

Simon: Great — can you paste the snippet where eviction starts? Even a short screencap of kernel list is fine. If it's the kernel selector, we may need to pin a fallback kernel for small sequence lengths.

Anya: Pasted a snippet from the timeline: the eviction call appears ~23.4s, followed by several small cudaMemcpyAsync calls and a 12ms gap on the worker thread. Looks like batching heuristic forced an unexpected split and the selector chose a slower matmul kernel.

Maria: Created a short repro with flags to force the small-seqlen path and will run both old/new selector to compare. Will upload two captures and label them `selector-old` and `selector-new`.

Jake: When we have both captures, do a diff of kernel names + cumulative launch time. `nsys stats` and the GUI timeline diff help. Also check NVTX annotations for batching boundaries — sometimes our prefix/KV cache hits cause a zero-token fast path that confuses batch sizing.

Simon: Thanks all. If we confirm selector regression, we should rollback the variant and add a small perf-test that does bursty KV workloads so it doesn't regress again. :thumbsup:
